source.matching: exact canonical Taxon string against 16 hosts contributing to the nine posthoc Host+ event cells

interpretation: SInAS provides an independent alien-species chronology for every focal host and shows that many of these hosts have documented alien histories extending well before modern butterfly records. This supports feasibility of an independent host clock but does not validate WGSRPD3-level lag estimates.
limitation: SInAS Location is frequently country/island scale rather than WGSRPD level 3 (for example United States rather than New York, Minnesota or Tennessee), and many target-region records lack first-record years. Therefore it cannot by itself establish the local host-arrival year for the temporal lag analysis.
decision: Use SInAS as an independent broad-scale chronology/sensitivity source only. Do not replace the WGSRPD3 host clock with country-level SInAS dates and do not interpret the posthoc 86-year GBIF lag as validated.
